title: "Result tables"
subtitle: "Every table the study produced, grouped by what it is about, with its contents open to inspection"

```{python}
#| label: preparacion
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == "docs" else Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "docs" / "study"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from report_helpers import kpis, show_table

DATA = ROOT / "docs" / "study" / "data"
EARLY = DATA / "v01"

# Tables are grouped by what they describe, not by when they were computed. The order of the rules
# matters: the first pattern that matches a file name wins, so the specific ones come first.
GROUPS = [
    ("Provenance, coverage and audits", r"dataflow|coverage_layers|_audit|_provenance|_check$|identifier"),
    ("Case definition and its sensitivity", r"^case_definition|^f80_f89|rett|^S7d_|^figS5_|variant"),
    ("Hospital records", r"^grd_|^burden_|^expanded_hospital|^expanded_deis|^clinical_|^Figure5_|^expanded_age"),
    ("Community programmes", r"^rem_|^a05_|^p2_|^expanded_a27"),
    ("Education and surveys", r"^pie_|^junaeb|^education_|^survey|^fig3c_"),
    ("Territory and spatial structure", r"^S3_|^S4_|communes_public|^Table_regional|regions"),
    ("Models and convergence between sources", r"^models_|^selected_models|^fig3b_|^central_|^Table_S7|correlations"),
    ("Figure inputs", r"^fig3a_|^fig3d_"),
]


def group_of(name):
    for title, pattern in GROUPS:
        if re.search(pattern, name):
            return title
    return "Other tables"


tables = sorted(DATA.glob("*.csv"))
grouped = {}
for path in tables:
    grouped.setdefault(group_of(path.name), []).append(path)

kpis([
    (str(len(tables)), "Result tables published with this report"),
    (str(len(grouped)), "Subjects they cover"),
    (str(len(list(EARLY.glob('*.csv')))), "Tables from the earliest analysis, on a different window"),
    ("3", "Tables withheld to protect small commune cells"),
])
```

This chapter holds every result table the study produced, read from `docs/study/data/`. They ship with
the repository, so each one can be opened, checked and reused without the source microdata. Each table
below unfolds to show its full contents.

The study was written over several rounds of revision. Each round added tables without ever changing one
that had already been computed, so what appears here is the union of all of them — a single result set,
not a sequence of drafts. That claim is checked rather than asserted: `scripts/audit_versions.py` hashes
every table of every round and compares them pairwise.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Three tables are deliberately withheld

Two commune-by-year tables and one commune-level analytic file carry cells with fewer than five cases
next to a commune identifier, which together can identify individuals. They are not published. What is
published instead is `communes_public.csv`, the same commune extract with the identifiers removed and
the small cells masked. Every territorial result in this report is computed from data at that level or
coarser.
:::

```{python}
#| label: inventario
#| output: asis
def render_group(title, paths):
    print(f"\n## {title}\n")
    rows = []
    for path in paths:
        frame = pd.read_csv(path)
        rows.append({"Table": path.name, "Rows": len(frame), "Columns": len(frame.columns),
                     "Size (KB)": round(path.stat().st_size / 1024, 1)})
    show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), f"{len(paths)} tables on {title.lower()}", {"Size (KB)": 1})
    print()
    for path in paths:
        frame = pd.read_csv(path)
        preview = frame.head(200).to_html(index=False, classes="table table-sm", border=0, na_rep="")
        more = "" if len(frame) <= 200 else f"<p class='table-note'>First 200 of {len(frame):,} rows.</p>"
        print(f"<details class='corpus-table'><summary><code>{path.name}</code> "
              f"<span class='muted'>{len(frame):,} rows × {len(frame.columns)} columns</span></summary>"
              f"{more}<div class='analysis-table'>{preview}</div></details>\n")

for title, _ in GROUPS + [("Other tables", None)]:
    if title in grouped:
        render_group(title, grouped[title])
```

## The earliest analysis

```{python}
#| label: nota-v01
#| output: asis
print("""
::: {.callout-important}
## These five tables are not comparable with the rest of the report

They come from the first analysis of this material, which covered **2017–2024** rather than 2019–2025 and
predates the split of the case definition into its two variants. Their counts are therefore built on a
different observation window and a different definition, and a reader should not place them side by side
with the tables above or read a trend across the two. They are published because they are part of the
record of what was found, not because they extend the series.
:::
""")
```

```{python}
#| label: tablas-tempranas
#| output: asis
CAPTIONS = {
    "tabla1": "Characteristics of the records, by period",
    "tabla2": "Annual series of records and persons, with standardised rates and 95% confidence intervals",
    "tabla3": "Regional distribution, with standardised rates and indirect ratios",
    "tabla4": "Ecological correlations between sources, by unit and period",
    "tabla5": "Summary indicators, by period",
}
for path in sorted(EARLY.glob("tabla*.csv")):
    frame = pd.read_csv(path)
    title = CAPTIONS.get(path.stem, path.stem)
    preview = frame.to_html(index=False, classes="table table-sm", border=0, na_rep="")
    print(f"<details class='corpus-table'><summary>{title} "
          f"<span class='muted'>(2017–2024 window, earlier case definition)</span></summary>"
          f"<div class='analysis-table'>{preview}</div></details>\n")
```
